Second deliverable of the data analysis. Deaths of residents of the 33 study municipalities during the warm seasons
(1 November to 31 March) of 2009 to 2020, from the death records of the
Department of Health Statistics and Information (DEIS), and the analytic
dataset of the space-time-stratified case-crossover design.

::: {.no-download}

| Requested | Where |
|---|---|
| Clean DEIS deaths dataset: non-accidental and cardiopulmonary causes (ICD-10), urban Santiago, warm seasons 2009-2020 | [Clean deaths dataset](#sec-deaths) |
| Case-crossover analytic dataset, stratified in time and space: three or four control days per death, same day of the week, month, year and municipality | [Case-crossover analytic dataset](#sec-case-crossover) |
| Exposure at lags 0 to 3 | [Exposure at lags 0 to 3](#sec-lagged-exposure) |
| Summary table of mortality | [Mortality summary](#sec-mortality-summary) |
| R scripts | [R scripts](#sec-scripts) |

:::

# Methodology {#sec-methodology}

```{r}
#| label: setup-methodology
#| include: false
# Every number quoted in the methodology is computed here, from the
# configuration and the outputs of the scripts
method <- list()
method$municipalities <- study_municipalities()
method$years <- get_param("study", "years")
method$extract_years <- unlist(get_param("deis_extract", "years"))
method$lags <- unlist(get_param("design", "lags_days"))
method$strata <- unlist(get_param("design", "control_strata"))
method$age_labels <- unlist(get_param("mortality", "age_labels"))
method$cause_groups <- get_param("mortality", "cause_groups")
method$flow <- read_table("mortality_flow.csv")
method$dataset <- read_table("case_crossover_summary.csv")
# One number of a table of steps or items, found by the start of its label
pick_value <- function(table, label_column, value_column, pattern) {
  value <- table[grepl(pattern, get(label_column)), get(value_column)]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}
flow_step <- function(pattern) pick_value(method$flow, "step", "deaths", pattern)
dataset_item <- function(pattern) pick_value(method$dataset, "item", "value", pattern)
stopifnot(identical(method$strata, c("municipality", "year", "month", "day_of_week")))
method$no_age_or_sex <- flow_step("^Non-accidental cause") - flow_step("with age and sex recorded")
```

*Scripts of this deliverable: `Code/20_mortality_deis.R` and
`Code/21_case_crossover_dataset.R`.
[Workflow and scripts](#sec-methods-workflow) lists what each one reads and
writes, and every part of the page names the scripts and the files behind its
tables and figures.*

## Aim and design {#sec-methods-aim}

This deliverable builds the outcome side of the study and joins it with the
exposure of [deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html): the deaths of the
residents of the study area, with their cause, age and sex, and the analytic
dataset on which the models of [deliverable 3](deliverable_3_models.html) are
fitted.

The design is a case-crossover study (Maclure, 1991) with referent days
stratified in time and space. Each death is compared with itself: the
exposure of the day of death against the exposure of other days of the same
person. What does not change within a few weeks (age, sex, chronic disease,
socioeconomic position, place of residence) is the same on the day of death
and on the control days, so it cannot confound the comparison. The control
days are all the days of the same municipality, calendar year, month and day
of the week as the day of death. Trend, season and the weekly cycle are
controlled by that choice, and the time-stratified scheme avoids the bias of
the schemes that choose control days around the day of death (Levy and
others, 2001; Janes and others, 2005).

## Population, period and unit {#sec-methods-population}

- **Population.** Residents of the `r nrow(method$municipalities)`
  municipalities of urban Santiago (the 32 of Santiago Province and Puente
  Alto), by the municipality of residence written in the death record.
- **Period.** Deaths in the warm seasons (1 November to 31 March) of
  `r method$years[1]` to `r method$years[2]`: January to March and November to
  December of each calendar year.
- **Unit.** The death. The deaths dataset has one row per death; the
  case-crossover dataset has one row per death and referent day.

## Data sources {#sec-methods-sources}

::: {.wide-table}

| Source | Producer | Content | Period of the file | How it reached the project | Used for |
|:-----|:------|:-----------|:-----|:------|:-----|
| Death records | Department of Health Statistics and Information (DEIS), Ministry of Health of Chile; official open-data file of deaths, <https://deis.minsal.cl> | One row per death: date, sex, age and its unit, municipality of residence, place of death, underlying cause (ICD-10) and, for injuries, external cause | Official file: 1990 to 2023. Extract used here: residents of the Metropolitan Region who died in `r method$extract_years[1]` to `r method$extract_years[2]`, `r fmt(flow_step("^Records in the input"))` records | Extract cut from the official file by `Code/05_deis_extract.R` | Deaths dataset |
| Exposure dataset | [Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-exposure-dataset), `Data/Derived/exposure_2009_2020.csv` | Temperature, heatwave indicators, ozone and co-pollutants by municipality and day | `r format(as.Date(sprintf("%d-01-01", method$years[1])) - max(method$lags))` to `r sprintf("%d-12-31", method$years[2])` | Written by `Code/13_exposure_merge_qc.R` | Exposure of the referent days, lags `r min(method$lags)` to `r max(method$lags)` |

: Sources of the data of this deliverable. {#tbl-sources}

:::

The death records are public and anonymous: they carry no name and no
identifier of the person. The file is kept as received in `Data/Input`, is
listed with its size and checksum in `Data/input_manifest.csv`, and the
scripts stop if the file they read is not the listed one. The scripts read
either the official file or an extract of it with the same columns.

## Selection of the deaths {#sec-methods-selection}

*Script: `Code/20_mortality_deis.R`. Every step is counted in
`Output/Tables/mortality_flow.csv`.*

1. Records with a date of death and a municipality of residence: `r fmt(flow_step("^With date of death"))` of the `r fmt(flow_step("^Records in the input"))` records of the input.
2. Residents of the `r nrow(method$municipalities)` study municipalities: `r fmt(flow_step("^Residents of"))` deaths.
3. Died in the study years: `r fmt(flow_step("^Died in [0-9]"))`.
4. Died in the warm season: `r fmt(flow_step("^Died in the warm season"))`.
5. Non-accidental cause: `r fmt(flow_step("^Non-accidental cause"))`. These are
   the deaths of the analysis.

Nothing is deleted at step 5: the deaths from other causes stay in the
dataset, flagged, so that every exclusion can be counted
([Source and selection](#sec-source-selection)).
`r fmt(method$no_age_or_sex)` non-accidental deaths have no age or no sex
recorded; they are part of the analyses of all the deaths and are missing only
from the analyses by age or by sex.

## Causes of death {#sec-methods-causes}

The cause of a death is its underlying cause (field `DIAG1`), coded with the
International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision (ICD-10). The groups
are those of the analysis plan, defined on the first three characters of the
code and written in `config/config.yml`. The script stops if a code does not
have the form of an ICD-10 code.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cause-groups
#| tbl-cap: "Cause groups of the analysis plan: ICD-10 codes of the underlying cause and deaths of the warm seasons of 2009 to 2020 in the study municipalities. A death can belong to several groups."
cause_table <- data.table(
  group = sub(" \\(.*$", "", cause_labels[names(method$cause_groups)]),
  codes = vapply(method$cause_groups, function(ranges) {
    paste(sub("^(.{3})-\\1$", "\\1", unlist(ranges)), collapse = ", ")   # I63-I63 is written I63
  }, character(1)),
  deaths = vapply(names(method$cause_groups), function(group) sum(deaths[[group]]), numeric(1))
)
kable(cause_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Cause group", "ICD-10 codes", "Deaths"))
```

Two kinds of death fall outside non-accidental mortality (A00 to R99):

- **Injuries**, coded S00 to T98 in the field of the underlying cause
  (`DIAG1`), with their external cause (V01 to Y98) in a second field
  (`DIAG2`). This is the exclusion that the plan asks for.
- **U codes**, which in these years are COVID-19 (U07.1 and U07.2). They are
  not named in the plan and fall outside the range A00 to R99; whether the
  months of the pandemic stay in the analysis is a
  [decision for the principal investigator](index.html).

## Age, sex and place of death {#sec-methods-attributes}

- **Age.** In completed years. An age recorded in months, days or hours is an
  age under one year. Groups of the plan:
  `r paste(method$age_labels, collapse = ", ")`.
- **Sex.** Male or female, as recorded; any other value counts as not
  recorded.
- **Place of death.** Home, hospital or clinic, or other. It is kept in the
  dataset and is not used in the models.

## Case-crossover dataset {#sec-methods-case-crossover}

*Script: `Code/21_case_crossover_dataset.R`; functions
`build_case_crossover()` and `lagged_exposure()` of `Code/01_functions.R`.*

**Referent days.** For death $i$, of a resident of municipality $m_i$ who
died on day $d_i$, the referent days are the days of the same calendar year
and month that fall on the same day of the week:

$$R_i = \left\{\, t : \ \mathrm{year}(t) = \mathrm{year}(d_i), \ \ \mathrm{month}(t) = \mathrm{month}(d_i), \ \ \mathrm{weekday}(t) = \mathrm{weekday}(d_i) \,\right\}.$$

The set holds the day of death and three or four control days, before and
after it. Each death is one stratum of the analysis; within it the variable
`case` is 1 on the day of death and 0 on the control days. The exposure is
that of the municipality of residence, so the stratum is defined in time and
in space. A month is either inside or outside the warm season: every control
day of a warm-season death is a warm-season day.

- Strata (deaths): `r fmt(dataset_item("^Deaths \\(strata\\)"))`.
- Rows (deaths and referent days): `r fmt(dataset_item("^Rows"))`.
- Deaths with three control days: `r fmt(dataset_item("with 3 control days"))`;
  with four: `r fmt(dataset_item("with 4 control days"))`.

**Exposure at lags `r min(method$lags)` to `r max(method$lags)`.** For
exposure variable $x$, the value at lag $k$ of day $t$ in municipality $m$ is
the value $k$ days earlier in the same municipality:

$$x^{(k)}_{m,t} = x_{m,\,t-k}, \qquad k = `r paste(method$lags, collapse = ", ")`.$$

The lag is applied to the day of death and to the control days alike. The
exposure dataset starts `r max(method$lags)` days before 1 January
`r method$years[1]` so that the first deaths of the period have their lagged
exposure. The lagged values are kept for the
`r fmt(dataset_item("^Municipality-days used as referent"))` municipality-days
that are a referent day of at least one death, in
`r fmt(dataset_item("^Lagged exposure columns"))` columns named
`<variable>_lag<k>`: the heatwave indicators, the high-ozone flags, the
temperature and the pollutant series.

**Two files.** `Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv` holds the strata and the
attributes of each death (sex, age group, cause groups);
`Data/Derived/exposure_lagged.csv` holds the lagged exposures. Joining them on
municipality and day gives the dataset of any model, for any definition of
the exposure ([Exposure at lags 0 to 3](#sec-lagged-exposure)).

## Checks {#sec-methods-checks}

A check that fails stops the script.

| Check | Where it is made |
|:----------------|:-------------|
| The input file is the one listed in the manifest (size and checksum) | `input_path()`, in every script |
| Every underlying cause has the form of an ICD-10 code; every age has a known unit | `Code/20_mortality_deis.R` |
| Every death has exactly one day of death and three or four control days among its referent days | `build_case_crossover()` |
| Every referent day is a day of the exposure dataset | `Code/21_case_crossover_dataset.R` |
| The exposure dataset has one row per municipality and day before it is lagged | `lagged_exposure()` |
| Referent days, lags and ICD-10 ranges give the known answer on small examples | `tests/test_methods.R` ([Method checks](#sec-method-checks)) |

: Checks of the deaths dataset and of the case-crossover dataset. {#tbl-checks}

`Code/run_all.R` runs the scripts in order, each in a new R session, and then
renders the pages. The scripts are not run when a page is rendered.

| Script | Reads | Writes | Parts of this page |
|:-------|:------|:--------------|:------|

| `Code/20_mortality_deis.R` | The extract of the death records | `Data/Derived/deaths_clean.csv`; `Output/Tables/mortality_flow.csv`, `mortality_excluded_causes.csv`, `mortality_by_cause_year.csv`, `mortality_by_municipality_year.csv` | Clean deaths dataset; mortality summary |
| `Code/21_case_crossover_dataset.R` | `deaths_clean.csv`; `Data/Derived/exposure_2009_2020.csv` | `Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv`, `exposure_lagged.csv`; `Output/Tables/case_crossover_summary.csv` | Case-crossover analytic dataset; exposure at lags 0 to 3 |
| `tests/test_methods.R` | Nothing: small examples built in the script | The list of checks shown in this page | Method checks |

Shared code: `Code/00_setup.R` (folders, configuration, checks of the
inputs) and `Code/01_functions.R` (the functions named above). All the
parameters are in `config/config.yml`. The code of every script is in
[R scripts](#sec-scripts).

## Limits {#sec-methods-limits}

- **The cause is the underlying cause of the death certificate.** Its coding
  has errors that this analysis cannot measure; the broad group of
  non-accidental mortality is less sensitive to them than the specific causes.
- **The exposure is that of the municipality of residence.** Where the person
  was on the days before death, and where the death occurred, are not known.
- **Small groups.** Some specific causes have few deaths (table above), and
  their estimates in deliverable 3 are imprecise.
- **COVID-19.** Its deaths are outside the non-accidental definition, and the
  warm-season months of 2020 are in the period: an open decision.
- **Counts, not rates.** The tables of this page count deaths. Population
  denominators enter with the attributable burden of deliverable 3.

## References {#sec-methods-references}

- Janes, H., Sheppard, L., and Lumley, T. (2005). Case-crossover analyses of
  air pollution exposure data: referent selection strategies and their
  implications for bias. *Epidemiology*, 16(6), 717-726.
- Levy, D., Lumley, T., Sheppard, L., Kaufman, J., and Checkoway, H. (2001).
  Referent selection in case-crossover analyses of acute health effects of air
  pollution. *Epidemiology*, 12(2), 186-192.
  <https://doi.org/10.1097/00001648-200103000-00010>.
- Maclure, M. (1991). The case-crossover design: a method for studying
  transient effects on the risk of acute events. *American Journal of
  Epidemiology*, 133(2), 144-153.
- Department of Health Statistics and Information (DEIS), Ministry of Health
  of Chile. Deaths, official figures, open data. <https://deis.minsal.cl>.

# Clean deaths dataset {#sec-deaths}

*Script: `Code/20_mortality_deis.R`. Dataset: `Data/Derived/deaths_clean.csv`.
Tables: `Output/Tables/mortality_flow.csv` and `mortality_excluded_causes.csv`.*

The dataset is `Data/Derived/deaths_clean.csv`, written by
`Code/20_mortality_deis.R`: one row per death, with the date, the municipality
of residence, sex, age, place of death, the underlying cause (ICD-10) and one
flag for each cause group of the analysis plan. Deaths outside non-accidental
mortality stay in the file, flagged, so that every exclusion can be counted.

## Source and selection {#sec-source-selection}

The input is the official DEIS file of deaths 1990-2023 (open data, one row per
death, with date, sex, age, municipality of residence and underlying cause).
The scripts read either that file or an extract of it with the same columns;
the run behind this page used the extract of residents of the Metropolitan
Region who died in 2009-2020.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flow
#| tbl-cap: "Records kept at each step of the selection."
flow <- read_table("mortality_flow.csv")
kable(flow, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), col.names = c("Step", "Deaths"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-excluded
#| tbl-cap: "Deaths outside non-accidental mortality (A00-R99), by calendar year."
excluded <- read_table("mortality_excluded_causes.csv")
kable(dcast(excluded, cause ~ year, value.var = "deaths", fill = 0),
      format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Non-accidental mortality follows the analysis plan: underlying cause between
A00 and R99. Two groups fall outside it. Injuries, coded S00-T98 with their
external cause in a second field, are the exclusion the plan asks for. The U
codes are COVID-19 (U07.1 and U07.2): `r fmt(excluded[grepl("COVID", cause), sum(deaths)])`
deaths in the warm-season months of 2020 are therefore not part of the
non-accidental series. Whether the months of the pandemic stay in the analysis
is a decision for the principal investigator.

`r fmt(deaths[age_years > 110, .N])` records have a recorded age above 110 years;
they stay in the oldest age group.

# Mortality summary {#sec-mortality-summary}

*Script: `Code/20_mortality_deis.R`. Tables:
`Output/Tables/mortality_by_cause_year.csv` and
`mortality_by_municipality_year.csv`. The table by age and sex, the series of
deaths per day and the maps are computed in this page from
`Data/Derived/deaths_clean.csv`.*

## By cause, age and sex

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cause-year
#| tbl-cap: "Deaths in the warm-season months by cause group and calendar year. The groups overlap: each sub-cause is part of its parent group."
cause_year <- read_table("mortality_by_cause_year.csv")
cause_wide <- dcast(cause_year, cause ~ year, value.var = "deaths", fill = 0)
cause_wide[, Total := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = setdiff(names(cause_wide), "cause")]
cause_wide <- cause_wide[match(names(cause_labels), cause)]
cause_wide[, cause := cause_labels[cause]]
kable(cause_wide, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-age-sex
#| tbl-cap: "Non-accidental deaths by age group and sex, warm seasons 2009-2020."
age_sex <- dcast(non_accidental[, .N, by = .(age_group, sex)], age_group ~ sex, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
age_sex[, total := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = setdiff(names(age_sex), "age_group")]
age_sex[, share := 100 * total / sum(total)]
kable(age_sex, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-daily
#| fig-cap: "Non-accidental deaths per day in the 33 municipalities by month of the warm season and calendar year."
#| fig-height: 3.8
daily <- non_accidental[, .N, by = date]
monthly <- daily[, .(per_day = mean(N)), by = .(year = year(date), month = month(date))]
monthly[, month := factor(month, levels = c(1, 2, 3, 11, 12),
                          labels = c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Nov", "Dec"))]
ggplot(monthly, aes(year, per_day)) +
  geom_line(colour = ramp_blue[6], linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = ramp_blue[6], size = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(~month, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2010, 2015, 2020)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Deaths per day")
```

## By municipality

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-deaths
#| fig-cap: "Non-accidental deaths per year in the warm-season months, 2009-2020, and share of deaths at ages 85 or more."
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 9
shapes_env <- new.env()
load(input_path("municipality_shapes"), envir = shapes_env)
shapes <- shapes_env$comunas_santiago[, "cod_comuna"]
shapes$com <- as.integer(shapes$cod_comuna)
by_mun <- non_accidental[, .(per_year = .N / 12, oldest = 100 * mean(age_group == "85+", na.rm = TRUE)),
                         by = com]
map_values <- function(column, title, legend, hue, digits) {
  ggplot(merge(shapes, by_mun, by = "com")) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = .data[[column]]), colour = "#ffffff", linewidth = 0.25) +
    scale_fill_magnitude(name = legend, hue = hue,
                         labels = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)) +
    labs(title = title) + theme_map()
}
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  map_values("per_year", "Deaths per year", "Deaths", "blue", 0),
  map_values("oldest", "Deaths at ages 85 or more", "%", "orange", 0), ncol = 2
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-municipality
#| tbl-cap: "Non-accidental deaths by municipality and calendar year, warm-season months."
mun_year <- read_table("mortality_by_municipality_year.csv")
mun_wide <- dcast(mun_year[group == "non_accidental"], municipality ~ year, value.var = "deaths", fill = 0)
kableExtra::scroll_box(
  kableExtra::kable_styling(kable(mun_wide, format = "html", format.args = list(big.mark = ",")),
                            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
  height = "380px"
)
```

The same table for every cause group, age group and sex is in
`Output/Tables/mortality_by_municipality_year.csv`. Counts are deaths, not
rates: population denominators enter with the attributable burden
(deliverable 3).

# Case-crossover analytic dataset {#sec-case-crossover}

*Script: `Code/21_case_crossover_dataset.R`, with the functions
`build_case_crossover()` and `lagged_exposure()` of `Code/01_functions.R`.
Datasets: `Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv` and `exposure_lagged.csv`. Table:
`Output/Tables/case_crossover_summary.csv`.*

Each non-accidental death is one stratum. Its referent days are all the days of
the same municipality, calendar year, month and day of the week: the day of
death and three or four control days. A month is either inside or outside the
warm season, so every control day is a warm-season day.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cc
#| tbl-cap: "Size of the case-crossover dataset."
kable(read_table("case_crossover_summary.csv"), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Item", "Value"))
```

```{r}
#| label: cc-example
cc <- fread(derived_path("case_crossover.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8", nrows = 9)
kable(cc[, .(id, com, case_date, date, case, sex, age_group, icd3)],
      caption = "First rows of case_crossover.csv: two deaths with their referent days.")
```

## Exposure at lags 0 to 3 {#sec-lagged-exposure}

`Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv` holds the structure and the attributes of
each death (sex, age group, cause flags). `Data/Derived/exposure_lagged.csv`
holds, for every municipality-day used as a referent, each exposure variable at
lags 0 to 3 (`<variable>_lag<k>` is the exposure k days earlier). Joining the two
on municipality and day gives the model dataset for any definition:

```r
library(survival)
cc <- fread("Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv")
lagged <- fread("Data/Derived/exposure_lagged.csv")
model_data <- merge(cc, lagged[, .(com, date, hw = hw_p95_2d_lag1, oz = o3_idw_gt_p75_lag1)],
                    by = c("com", "date"))
clogit(case ~ hw + oz + strata(id), data = model_data)
```

# Method checks {#sec-method-checks}

*Script: `tests/test_methods.R`, run here and at the start of every run of
`Code/run_all.R`.*

`tests/test_methods.R` checks the functions behind this page and the models of
deliverable 3
against independent calculations: the referent selection, the lagging, the
equivalence between the fit on individual records and the faster weighted fit
used in the models, the recovery of known odds ratios from simulated deaths,
and the delta-method intervals against `msm::deltamethod`.

```{r}
#| label: method-checks
#| code-summary: "Run tests/test_methods.R"
checks <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
                  shQuote(here::here("tests", "test_methods.R")), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
if (!is.null(attr(checks, "status"))) stop(paste(checks, collapse = "\n"))
cat(grep("^ok|^All|simulated", checks, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```
